title: Auditing Operational Resilience and Third Parties
summary: How to audit the firm's ability to withstand and recover from disruption, including important business services, cyber security, outsourcing and reliance on critical third parties.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to audit the firm's ability to withstand and recover from disruption, including important business services, cyber security, outsourcing and reliance on critical third parties.
Learning Objectives: Assess the mapping of important business services and impact tolerances
Audit cyber, incident management and scenario testing arrangements
Evaluate outsourcing and third-party risk management across the lifecycle
Syllabus: Important business services, mapping and impact tolerances
Cyber security, incident response and business continuity, including ISO 22301
Outsourcing and third-party due diligence, contracts, oversight and exit
Concentration risk and reliance on intragroup and cloud providers
Intended Audience: Heads of internal audit, audit managers and auditors in banks, insurers, investment firms, fund managers and payment firms
Co-sourced and outsourced audit providers delivering assurance to regulated firms
Audit committee members and compliance and risk staff who rely on internal audit work
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of internal audit, risk or compliance in a regulated firm is helpful. No specialist technical background is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, The Internal Audit Function in Banks (2012)
Institute of Internal Auditors, Global Internal Audit Standards (2024)
Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
